title: Lorenzo Mansutti (Estates plumber), Discussion regarding Judge's Directions to the Jury

blocks.text: 14 June 2023
Defence witness Lorenzo Mansutti Discussion regarding Judge's directions to the jury
CONTENTS
MR LORENZO MANSUTTI (sworn)
Examination-in-chief by MR MYERS
Cross-examination by MR JOHNSON
Discussion
Wednesday, 14 June 2023
(Delay in proceedings)
(In the absence of the jury)
My Lord, thank you for the time that we had.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: There was a matter that arose that we had to deal with, so we're grateful for that.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: There is one witness that we'll be calling. If I could hand a copy of the statement, which is provided to us by the prosecution, and the documents that accompany that. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: I'm just asked to remind the court for the purpose of your Lordship's record, today is Day 129. It may be that when your Lordship is referencing with the transcripts we're not sure if that's caught up with it or not, but today is Day 129 to assist your Lordship, that's where we're up to.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: There is the one witness to call and then we'll be in a position to close the case.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (In the presence of the jury)
Good morning, members of the jury.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I apologise for the delay in starting proceedings today and for the fact that you were brought up and then had to be taken back down, but something arose rather last minute, but we're now in a position to proceed.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: My Lord, we will shortly be closing the case for Ms Letby, but before we do that, just so the jury understand, there is a witness to be called who deals with a discrete issue that arose in the course of her evidence and that related to sanitation at the hospital.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: With that in mind, could we please call Mr Mansutti to give evidence?
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: MR LORENZO MANSUTTI (sworn)
Examination-in-chief by MR MYERS
Would you like take a seat? Would you give your name, full name, for the jury, please?
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Lorenzo Mansutti.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: I'd ask you if you can keep your voice loud. I'm sure you will. If you aim it towards the back row of the jury, then we can all hear you and no one is going to think you are speaking too loudly. That is never the complaint in here. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Could you tell the ladies and gentlemen of the jury what the nature of your employment is?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yeah, I work at the Countess of Chester Hospital. I'm now estates supervisor, but I was estates plumber, since about 1986 when I started.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Right. And were you working there between 2015 through to 2016?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, I was.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: All right. You made a statement in these proceedings, haven't you, a witness statement?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Don't worry about looking at us, if you look to the ladies and gentlemen, they can hear you the better for that. That statement was dated -- was it 26 May this year?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I believe it was, yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: So a few weeks ago?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: And when were you first asked to make that witness statement, roughly?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I think it was a day or so earlier. Maybe the day before.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: All right. Some a day or so before 26 May. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Who asked you to do that?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It was my line manager who asked me.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Who wanted to speak to you to take the statement? Do you recall who? Was it a police officer?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It was two police officers, sorry, yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: So they came along to take a statement from you at that point?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's correct, yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: That statement was to deal with what? Do you remember what it was they were interested in?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It was questions around the plumbing and the sewage system of the Women and Children's Building.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Right. I'm going to ask you a little bit about that if you can help us.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: How up to date was the plumbing and sewage system -- was it at the Countess of Chester Hospital?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Which area of the Countess of Chester Hospital were you looking at?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I think this is the Women and Children's Building.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Does that include the neonatal unit?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It does, yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: So how up to date was that at the time we're looking at, back in 2015 to 2016?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Um, I believe it was originally built in the late 60s, opened 1970s, so there'd been some improvement works over that time.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Were there any particular issues with the pipework which was in place?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, there was issues with the drainage system.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: What sort of problems emerged that you had to deal with?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Um... Sort of various blockages. You know, times where the cast iron would crack -- it was all cast iron pipe and the cast iron would crack due to a number of reasons, expansion, contraction or just age, I think.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Just to help us, if there's a pipe in a system like this and it blocks, what can happen to the water or the sewage that would otherwise be going down that pipe?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It comes up the next lowest point, really.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Right. And where would it come up through, what sort of places do you find --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It could come up through toilets or a wash hand basin, anywhere where there's an open outlet, really.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Did that happen from time to time, there'd be a blockage and then --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: And sewage or water might come up through another unit somewhere?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Did you get leaks there ever?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, there were occasionally, yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: If there was an incident with sanitation like that, what would you or your staff be called upon to do?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Normally, a call would come through to the help desk — and the nature of where it was, we'd sort of attend immediately to try and rectify the issues as quickly as possible.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: And how often were you called to deal with these sort of issues?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Through the whole building it was... It was more...
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: weekly, I guess.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Are we talking about 1986 onwards, when he started, or are we talking about 2015/2016?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I'm focusing on 2015 to 2016. Can I check: is that right, Mr Mansutti.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, I would guess weekly.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: I'm grateful, my Lord. If I wasn't clear about that, I apologise.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: You understand I am asking you about 2015/2016, Mr Mansutti.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: (No audible answer).
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Thank you. So maybe weekly you'd be dealing with something?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, more often than not.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: When the officers came to speak to you about this were they interested in specifically things that had happened in the neonatal unit by way of blockage or leakage?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, they asked -- an occasion where we had a blockage in the central labour suite, which is next door adjacent and...
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: We're going to have a look at a plan in a moment and you can talk us through it. Before we do that, the incident you are talking about, we're going to look at a number of incidents, but this incident, can you tell us what happened and what went where?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: To be honest, I don't think I actually attended this particular one, I think it was my colleague. But I think the drainage system had backed up and the wash hand basin, which is in nursery 1 --
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: We'll take it step by step: nursery 1 in which part of the hospital?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: The neonatal.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: The neonatal unit, okay. So something had backed up in the pipe?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes. I guess it'd backed up the wash hand basin and that's when we got the -- or the department got the call to --
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: What happened with the wash hand basin, what came out of it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I guess it was foul water out of the drain.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Right. And to someone who isn't engaged in your line of work, foul water might mean water that isn't very nice, but you actually mean something by foul water, don't you?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, foul is a generic term of what goes down toilets and wash hand basins and so forth.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: It could be human waste?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Sewage?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: So foul water backed up. And where did it come out in nursery 1?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I believe it came out of the wash hand basin.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: In the neonatal unit?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Do you recall precisely when during 2015 to 2016 that happened?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I don't, I'm sorry, no.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Do you know where the water had come from, the foul water?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That particular section of drainage comes from ward 32, which is the ward above the neonatal unit. So it would have come from that area.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: All right. When the officers came, did they show you any Datix reports?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, they did.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: And they showed you one for the system dated 26 January 2016, didn't they? We're going to have a look at it in a minute.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: But do you remember, there was a couple, wasn't there?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: There was two.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: And one of them falls in the date range we're looking at. So you had an opportunity to look at that, Mr Mansutti. Can I show it to you again and just have a look at what it was you dealt with on that occasion?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Certainly.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: I'm going to ask Mr Murphy please to put up the Datix form, which is at D35. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Have a look at the screen, Mr Mansutti. Just enlarge it a little bit, please. I just ask for your input on what we have here. Can I ask, are you familiar with the way the Datix system works?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: All right. We've got a ID number for the incident.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Can you see 137935?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: And can you help us, can you see where the reported date is? Just a few lines down.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: All right. 26 January 2016. Scroll down to see the location of what it was you were called to deal with.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So in the neonatal unit?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Thank you. And if we go down to see the type of incident, can you help us, just looking there, at what it was you were dealing with as it is entered into the form?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Um... The category was environment, I guess that's the category on the actual drop-down box on the Datix, and subcategory flood.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: If we scroll down over the page we can get a little more detail. So we've got 26 January 2016. We can see the time 02.30. Does that mean, so far as you're aware, the time this was identified?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, I think that was probably the time that the issue was identified on the unit and potentially when they instigated the --
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: All right.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: -- call-out procedure, maybe, or was that a bit later --
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: We'll have a look in the entry. Description:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Nursery 4 currently closed due to plumbing work/deep cleaning of nursery. Lights therefore off inside nursery and door kept ajar. Member of staff walking past nursery at approximately 02.30 noticed glistening upon the floor. Lights switched on and floor noted to be completely flooded. Mixer tap was switched on and sink completely blocked. Domestic supervisor bleeped and informed of flooded floor. Attempt made to clear blockage with forceps. One piece of white cloth extracted, which appeared to have been forced in. Water within sink noted to contain much black debris. Sink still blocked however. Tap lever secured to off position as best as possible with a length of oxygen tubing. Floor cleared by night domestic.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Nursery noted to be flooded again at approximately 04.30. Mixer tap lever had sprung out to very slightly on position and floor almost completely flooded again. Domestic supervisor informed. Bed coordinator informed who advised to bleep the on-call plumber. Same performed. Plumber arrived 05.50. Managed to suction 2 further pieces of white cloth from plughole. Sink now draining. Tap lever also fixed."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Do you recall anything in particular about that incident?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No, I don't. I think it was my colleague who actually attended on that night.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: So we can be quite clear, that's different from the incident in nursery 1 where you described foul water coming through the sink?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: And just for our purposes, can we scroll down, Mr Murphy, to see who reported that incident? We know from these forms, Mr Mansutti, there is a section for the incident reporter and, just so the jury can follow this, we can see that's reported by someone called Mr Christopher Booth who's a neonatal practitioner.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Thank you. We can take that down, thank you, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: When you are called to attend plumbing or sewage incidents in the hospital, is there something called a service report that is completed to keep a record of what happened?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes. More often than not. Not every time.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: All right. I'm going to go through a number of them that we've been provided with and, since it's dealt with by you or your department, I'm going to ask you to assist us with what we have in them. Is that all right?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: There's about 10 of them. I'm going to ask Mr Murphy to put up on the screen a document. As it happens, as we'll see, we've got these documents in the order that they were given to us here. They're not actually in date order. So if everyone can bear with me, I'm going to ask Mr Murphy to take us through them so they are in date...
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I'll ask Mr Murphy to take us through them in date order. If we start in date order. Can you help us, are you familiar with this type of form?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: So a service report. Can you help us with how it is this form is put together?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: What normally happens is we have the estates help desk and whenever there's a fault that occurs in the trust, the telephone number or email will come through and if it's normally urgent -- sorry, if it's urgent they normally ring up rather than email because it needs attention sort of straightaway. That then gets logged on the system, the FM First system, a system we still use, albeit an updated version.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Thank you. The information we need to look at is in the top half of these forms as they're on the screen, so we'll just
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: have a look at what we have. Can you help us, first of all, then with the date that this assistance was requested?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Date requested is 4/7/2015.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: So 4 July 2015. We can see that on the right-hand side underneath the bar code; is that right?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: That's where you get that from?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Okay. Thank you. When an incident comes in, is it allocated to a particular member of the estate staff?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, we've got all trades and assistance as well, so the estates officer or the help desk will determine.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: And this is allocated to C Clark.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's my colleague, Chris Clark.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Thank you. Can you help us with where this incident is that's reported to you, the actual location in the hospital?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: The location says ward 35, which is the central labour suite.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: We'll have a look at the plan in a moment for you to help us, but just so the jury can follow, "Ward 35 CLS", if you follow down on the right-hand side it's in the large box at the bottom in the middle, the word "location" with "Ward 35 CLS" next to it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Correct, yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Can I just check you can see that, ladies and gentlemen?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: The forms follow this standard format, so once we have done this, it'll be quicker.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Pausing there, if we come out of the form I'm going to put a plan on the screen for you to help us with where ward 35 is, Mr Mansutti.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: We'll come back to this sheet in a moment, but if we could have the plan, please, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: We're all familiar particularly with what we have on the lefthand side of the screen here, which is the neonatal unit and those parts of the hospital closest to it. So you take a look for a moment just to get your eye in on the plan.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: And can you orientate yourself to that? So where we see reference to CLS, which is the central labour suite, can you help us with what area of the hospital that is?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yeah, we've got the left-hand plan, if you like --
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: -- which is --
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Do you want to use that mouse next to you? If it's on you can show us with that.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So we've got left-hand section there which equates to sort of that area there (indicating), I guess. That's the courtyard. That's consistent with that.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So central labour suite is, from the main entrance, all that area there.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: All right. Ward 35 of the central labour suite, can you help us with where that would be?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It's the same unit. 35 is central labour suite.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: It's the whole of that area?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Does the pipework run from there to where? From the central labour suite, where does it run to?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Pretty much all over. If we've got ward 32, which is above... So all the waste pipes will run --
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: All right.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: -- down into the unit and then into the underslab drainage and ultimately outside.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Did you say ward 32 is above --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Ward 32, which is above neonatal.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: So that's the ward above neonatal?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: And what's the ward below called? Is that ward 35?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, that's 35 CLS, which is the same unit.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: So 35 is downstairs and 32 is upstairs?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Thank you for that. We can go back then just to the report that we have. If we go back to the first page of the service reports, please, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: We have a series of reports dealing with the CLS, the central labour suite, and the neonatal unit. We're just going to have a look at them now.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: What was the problem that Mr Clark was called out to deal with on 4 July 2015?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Well, the detail on the report says, "Blocked drain CLS", so again that could be anywhere on that unit.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Thank you. "Blocked drains in the CLS", that's specifically ward 35, is it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: The downstairs part?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Thank you. If there's a blocked drain somewhere, what happens to the water in the system? Can you say or do you not know?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Sorry, which?
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: If the drain is blocked, water that would otherwise go out, where does it go to?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It just continues to flow into the drain, if it's still in use, unless it's put out of order.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Could we go to the second page then of this? This is 8 August 2015; is that right?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Allocated to you?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Mm-hm.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: And what was the incident you dealt with on 8 August 2015?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Again, the detail says, "Flood in CLS".
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: It says ward 35, doesn't it --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: -- if you look on the right-hand side?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: So a flood in the downstairs ward of the CLS?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Thank you. Can we go to page 3, please?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Sorry, just a puzzle. When you say 8 August, the planned date says 10 August.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: "Date requested" I'm looking at, my Lord, at the top. "Date requested." Then if we look at the bottom left-hand corner it's got "call out" and your name, Mr Mansutti, hasn't it?
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: That's correct.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: And does that assist us with what actually, so we can be quite clear, the date is that you were called out?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It would have been the 8th (overspeaking) --
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: So you're called out on the 8th and then you say, "We'll do the work on the 10th or plan to do the work on the 10th"?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: No, that would have been --
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Someone does.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: -- repaired, yeah.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: Sorry, it was me being stupid.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Not at all, my Lord. There are a number of dates here. Certainly the date that the incident is reported is 8 August.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: I can see that at the very bottom.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Page 3, then, please. We move to October, 2 October 2015. Is this the same location that we're dealing with?
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: What's the issue on this occasion?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Again, blocked drains on ward 35 CLS.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: All right. We're going to go through in date order, which means we need to go next to page 7, Mr Murphy, which takes us to 6 August, 6 August 2015 -- sorry, 6 October 2015. Can you help us with the location of this particular incident?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, that's in the neonatal unit.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: All right. What was it that you were called out to deal with on 6 October 2015 in the neonatal unit?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: To investigate floods. So that could have been a number of --
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: All right (overspeaking). When it says flood though, so no one can be in any doubt, we're not talking about floods as a result of rainwater coming in?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Possibly.
blocks.speaker: MANSUTTI

blocks.text: So whereas in the missing body murder case it is inherently suspicious that something like that has happened, it is not inherently suspicious that a baby on a neonatal unit might become unwell. In itself it isn't.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: In itself, isolated occasions or some occasions occurring, but I think we're -- I understand what your point is, Mr Myers, but I am not going to direct the jury that they have to be sure, for example in the case of [Baby A], for argument's sake, which actually is quite a clear one in the sense --
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: The allegation is.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: The allegation is clear that there was intravenous injection of air. But in relation to other ones where there are -- the differential diagnosis, everything else is excluded, so to speak, of known reasons, and then there are these other possible reasons, distended stomach and things like that, or vomiting, which indicates it may have been milk, they don't have to decide, well, it was definitely air that was put down the stomach or it was definitely milk that was put down the stomach. That's what I'm trying to avoid and that's when I'm saying precisely how.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Very well.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: It's the point we made in our response to the submission of no case at paragraph 22 of our response.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Your Lordship has, partially at least, repeated, no doubt unwittingly, what we said. We mentioned no-body murder cases.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Well, I was just thinking of my experience of no-body murder cases.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Absolutely, but it's paragraph 22. We make the point that in our -- well, how we phrased it then was:
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: "In all the cases in relation to which the application of the submissions of no case were being made, the treating and expert medical practitioners have all said that in their view there was no natural, non-criminal cause for the child's collapse. That in itself and independently of the evidence of air embolus is sufficient evidence on which a jury may properly consider the question of Lucy Letby's liability. It is not necessary for the prosecution to prove how the children died or what precise mechanism caused their collapses, only that the killings were unlawful, at the hands of the accused, and at the time she had the requisite intention."
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: And the most obvious example of that as a proposition was a murder case in which there is no body.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Well, there we are. All right. Again, I will draft something. I'm not going to invite anyone else to draft anything in relation to that. I will draft something to which you can both respond. So Mr Myers, I'm mindful of your submissions in relation to that and I will consider them and the way in which, where appropriate, they can be accommodated.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I'm grateful, my Lord.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Right. Anything else? No? Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Just to confirm, the court will be sitting at 10 o'clock tomorrow. The jury will not be here until 12 o'clock. Thank you very much. Does anyone --
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes, we would like a visit with Ms Letby if we may, please.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: A visit before the defendant leaves the building, please. Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you, my Lord.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS
